query: GPU cloud provider raises or cuts GPU rental prices per hour

results.title: fal raises serverless H100 rate to $2.49/hr, adds GB200 GPU, doubles MiniMax video pricing — PricingSaaS Pulse
highlights:
## What changed

fal's serverless GPU pricing moved across the board: H100 instances rose from $1.89 to $2.49 per hour (up 32%), B300 instances rose from $4.49 to $5.99 per hour (up 33%), and a new GB200 GPU tier was added to the lineup. Separately, MiniMax's H3 Max video model saw its per-second generation rate double, from $0.025 to $0.05.

...

For teams building on fal, this is a direct cost-of-goods increase on two of its most-used GPU tiers plus a 2x jump on one of its video models - margin that has to be absorbed or passed through to end customers. For fal, layering in GB200 support signals it's racing to keep pace with Nvidia's newest hardware generation while monetizing the older fleet harder. Watch whether this is the start of a broader repricing across fal's remaining GPU and model catalog, given it's now made three pricing moves in ten weeks, or whether this settles back into the roughly 30-day cadence its track record shows.

...

This is fal's third real pricing change since tracking began in late July — coming just a day after it finished filling out its Audio and 3D model API price lists on Oct 1 — and its second GPU rate hike since the H100 list price moved to $4.50/hr in early August. Price increases are everywhere in the index right now: Shipday's Enterprise tier jumped 40%, Cumul raised its USD plan 25%, and Hedra hiked its Individual plan all landed in the same late-September window. Most of those are SaaS seat pricing; fal's move extends the same pressure to raw GPU-hour and per-second inference rates, the cost layer underneath everyone else's AI pricing.

results.title: Nebius and CoreWeave Lift Nvidia GPU Prices by Up to 21% - Economic Frame
highlights:
Nvidia rental prices are rising even for last-generation H100s. Nebius has posted an October 1, 2026 on-demand card that lifts selected Nvidia GPU-hour rates by 16.9% to 21.0%. CoreWeave said on September 17 that it is still signing compute at higher prices, including short contracts at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue. A landlord can charge more for a chip it does not make only while that chip stays scarce. That is the signal behind Nvidia, and it is the opposite of a capacity glut.

Nebius’s price page, checked on October 2, still prints two columns. On-demand H100 is $3.85 per GPU-hour. The column marked effective October 1 is $4.50. The same split runs through the H200, the B200, and the B300. Reuters reported on September 17 that this was the second pay-as-you-go increase in about three months, with selected Nvidia GPU rates up 17% to 21%. The card on nebius.com/prices matches that range. It does not show every customer already paying the new rate.

...

Four Nvidia rows have a public before and after. GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 racks are still “contact us” in both columns. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. L40S “from” rates do not move. The hike lands on the accelerators customers are queued for.

| Nvidia GPU | Prior on-demand column | Announced October 1 card | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HGX H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | +$0.65, or 16.9% |
| HGX H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | +$0.90, or 20.0% |
| HGX B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | +$1.35, or 18.9% |
| HGX B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | +$1.65, or 21.0% |

Reuters’ “17% to 21%” is this range, with 16.9% rounded up. “Up to 21%” is the B300. The smaller H100 move is the one that changes the reading. Hopper is not the generation Nvidia is leading with. A prior-generation accelerator getting more expensive to rent is not what surplus hardware looks like.

Put the H100 on a bill. Eight GPUs go from $30.80 an hour to $36.00. Over a 720-hour month the list charge goes from $22,176 to $25,920. An 8-GPU B300 box moves from $45,216 to $54,720. Those are walk-up numbers, before tax, storage, or a commitment discount, and they are not invoices.

...

Commitment discounts can run up to 35% below on-demand for large clusters reserved for multiple months. Full discount on the new H100 card is $2.93 an hour, under the old $3.85 list. On the new B300 card it is $6.18, under $7.85. “Up to” is not “everyone gets.” The headline increase is the unreserved rate.

Spot is a third price. Preemptible rates can change every 15 minutes, and the ceiling sits one cent under on-demand, but the printed floor is $0.79 on H100 and H200 and $0.99 on B200 and B300. An interruptible job is not paying $4.50. The October card is about firm capacity. Most revenue is priced as annual contract value per megawatt, not off this page.

...

CoreWeave did not publish an H100 card. On September 17 it published a contract print. The release, carried on Nasdaq, says that since June 30, 2026, CoreWeave has continued to contract new compute at higher prices. In the third quarter it has signed short-dated contracts of about three to six months, “with pricing of approximately $40 million per megawatt, calculated as annualized revenue divided by power required to service the related clusters.”

...

The third public card is Amazon Web Services capacity blocks. They are reservations, not on-demand. Checked on October 2, the AWS tables price an eight-GPU instance and, in parentheses, the rate per accelerator.

In US East the reserved accelerator rates checked on October 2 are $5.191 for an H100 (p5.48xlarge, eight GPUs at $41.528 an instance-hour, Northern Virginia and Ohio), $5.97 for an H200 on p5e in Ohio, $6.865 for an H200 on p5en in Northern Virginia, $12.355 for a B200, and $14.04 for a B300. Tokyo’s p5 H100 rate is $4.720, under Nebius’s new card, so the geography matters. Against the US East reservation, Nebius’s October 1 card is still cheaper: $4.50 versus $5.191, $5.40 versus $5.97 or $6.865, $8.50 versus $12.355, and $9.50 versus $14.04. CoreWeave published no GPU-hour, so it cannot be ranked here. The table is AWS capacity-block pricing.

Effective October 7, AWS says capacity-block rates per accelerator across available regions will be $5.970 on P5, $6.866 on P5e, $7.895 on P5en, $14.208 on P6-B200, and $16.146 on P6-B300, higher in GovCloud. On the US East H100 line, $5.191 to $5.970 is 15.0% on that reservation rate only. The same notice leaves on-demand and Savings Plan prices unchanged.

The products are not the same hour. Nebius on-demand can be started and stopped if the GPUs are free. An AWS capacity block is reserved in advance and paid up front at the rate in force when it is bought. Even with that difference, the hyperscaler’s reserved H100 in US East sits above Nebius’s new list, and Amazon has scheduled the reserved rate higher on October 7 while leaving on-demand unchanged.

...

A glut runs the other way. The owner of empty halls cuts the rate to fill them. Nebius is adding halls and raising the walk-up rate in the same season.

results.title: Nebius Vs CoreWeave: Which AI Stock Has the Upper Hand?
highlights:
## CoreWeave Has Less Cushion for GPU Pricing to Slip

That leaves CoreWeave with less room if GPU pricing slips, although any pricing hit would have a gradual impact as much of CoreWeave’s revenue is locked into multi-year contracts that reprice only when they renew. 

That is why the 2027–2029 renewal pricing cycle matters for CoreWeave. This also impacts Nebius as prepayments fund its capex, but don’t protect its rental rates, and its on-demand pricing can move quickly in either direction. Nebius has more room to absorb a price decline without taking on more debt for financing capex spend.

...

## GPU Rental Prices Are Rising, Even for Older H100s

GPU rental prices are rising across the board, and not just for the newer chips. Nebius is raising its H100 on-demand rental price by 17%, from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, starting October 1, 2026. 

This marks Nebius’ second price increase this year for the H100s, following an average 29% on-demand increase in May. It is also raising on-demand rentals of the H200, B200 and B300 by 20%, 19% and 21%, respectively. Rental prices for Nvidia’s B300 have seen a larger increase, up around 56% from its pre-May level of roughly $6.10 per hour. 

Nebius increased pricing across Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU instances by 17% to 21% effective Oct. 1. Rising rental rates across multiple GPU generations suggest AI infrastructure demand remains strong and support the thesis that older GPUs may retain economic value longer than many investors expect.

Nebius is not alone in increasing rental pricing for older GPUs. In September, CoreWeave stated that it is contracting new compute capacity at higher prices, while its Q2 earnings call mentioned a six-year old A100 GPU contract running into 2029. As confirmed by CEO Mike Intrator, pricing for prior-generation products is “at or above where it was years ago.”

...

But it doesn’t settle the depreciation debate. Some of the increase may reflect scarcity rather than durable value: the current HBM and DRAM memory bottlenecks and constrained B300 supply can push up the demand on older chips. Despite the reasons behind the current demand for older GPUs, the real test for neocloud economics lies in their renewal pricing during the final years of this decade.

highlights:
📌 Nebius GPU rental price hike takes effect October 1: H100 +17% to $4.50/hr, H200 +20% to $5.40/hr, B200 +19% to $8.50/hr, B300 +21% to $9.50/hr. Meanwhile, H100 one-year lease contracts have risen nearly 40% from $1.70/hr (Oct 2025) to $2.35/hr (Mar 2026), with domestic B300 spot prices reaching 14.5 million RMB per unit.

...

Three structural shifts are evident: first, compute leasing has become the primary financing vehicle for frontier AI, with Tencent ($7B), NVIDIA ($50B), and Broadcom-Anthropic ($42B) all using lease structures to bypass capex constraints. Second, chipmakers are vertically integrating into data center ownership — NVIDIA's Beacon Point lease signals that GPU supply is now tied to physical infrastructure control. Third, sustained price escalation (Nebius +17-21% effective today, H100 +40% YoY) confirms that demand structurally outpaces supply for the foreseeable future.

results.title: Amazon is hiking chip-rental prices and reportedly moving Nvidia processors off the balance sheet
highlights:
In a sign of the financing crunch facing the hyperscalers backing the AI revolution, Amazon has announced it is raising prices on how much it charges to rent high-performance microchips as it reportedly is going to sell and then lease back Nvidia chips.

Amazon AMZN on Friday said it is raising prices, by about 15%, starting next week, for what’s called EC2 Capacity Blocks, which provide access to computing power on Nvidia chips ranging from the older A100 to the newer, more high-performance B300.

results.title: GPU Prices 2026: H100 From $3.49/hr, RTX 5070 at +58%
highlights:
Renting one NVIDIA H100 for an hour costs $3.49 on Runpod and $12.29 on Microsoft Azure — the same chip, listed on public pricing pages on October 2, 2026. Axis Intelligence Research’s GPU Hour Premium Ratio puts the hyperscaler list premium at 2.93x the neocloud median, and AWS is raising every GPU Capacity Block rate by roughly 15% on October 7.

## Quick Answer

How much does a GPU cost in October 2026? In the cloud, an NVIDIA H100 lists between $3.49 and $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand; the neocloud median is $3.99. A B200 lists from $6.69 to $8.60. On the consumer side, the cheapest new RTX 5070 on Newegg was $869.99 against a $549 launch price — 58% above MSRP.

...

1. According to Axis Intelligence Research, hyperscalers list the NVIDIA H100 at 2.93 times the neocloud median price — $11.68 versus $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, as of October 2, 2026 (GPU Hour Premium Ratio, GHPR).
2. AWS raises EC2 Capacity Block GPU rates about 15% effective October 7, 2026, taking an H100 accelerator-hour from $5.191 to $5.970 and a B200 from $12.355 to $14.208, per AWS’s pricing page.
3. An 8-GPU H100 server rented on-demand for three years costs $2.58 million on Azure and $734,000 on Runpod, according to Axis Intelligence Research’s list-price TCO calculation.
4. The cheapest new GeForce RTX 5070 on Newegg cost $869.99 on October 2, 2026, 58% above the $549 price NVIDIA announced at CES in January 2025.
5. Azure’s spot price for an 8x H100 VM is 82% below its own on-demand rate — $18.17 versus $98.32 per hour in US East, per Microsoft’s Retail Prices API.

## How Much Does It Cost to Rent an H100 GPU per Hour?

The H100 is the reference chip for AI compute pricing, and in October 2026 its price depends far more on who rents it to you than on the silicon.

### H100 on-demand price per GPU-hour by provider (October 2, 2026)

| Provider | Instance / SKU | Listed price | GPUs | Price per GPU-hour | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod | H100 SXM Pod (Secure Cloud) | $3.49/hr | 1 | $3.49 | Runpod pricing |
| Lambda | NVIDIA H100 SXM instance | $3.99/GPU/hr | 1–8 | $3.99 | Lambda pricing |
| CoreWeave | NVIDIA HGX H100 (North America) | $49.24/hr | 8 | $6.16 | CoreWeave pricing |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g, us-central1 | $88.49/hr | 8 | $11.06 | Google Cloud accelerator-optimized pricing |
| Microsoft Azure | ND96isr H100 v5, East US | $98.32/hr | 8 | $12.29 | Azure Retail Prices API |

Per-GPU-hour figures for 8-GPU instances are Axis Intelligence Research calculations: instance price ÷ 8. Google Cloud and Azure prices include the host vCPUs, memory and local SSD bundled into the VM; neocloud prices also bundle host resources, but in smaller amounts per GPU.

The spread from cheapest to most expensive is 3.5x ($12.29 ÷ $3.49). That is the number most “GPU price” pages quote, and it overstates the useful comparison, because Runpod’s $3.49 Pod and Azure’s $98.32 VM are not the same product. Azure sells an eight-GPU VM with its host CPU, memory and storage bundled in; a single Pod is a single GPU.

...

### What does AWS charge for an H100?

AWS’s per-accelerator figure that we verified is the EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML rate — a reservation you book for a fixed window, not open-ended on-demand. On October 2, 2026 the p5.48xlarge (8x H100) Capacity Block rate in US East (N. Virginia) was $41.528 per instance-hour, or $5.191 per H100. AWS’s pricing page states that from October 7, 2026, the P5 rate becomes $5.970 per accelerator across all available regions. Axis Intelligence Research did not verify a current AWS on-demand p5 rate for this snapshot, so AWS is excluded from the on-demand table rather than estimated.

## Why Is AWS Raising GPU Prices in October 2026?

AWS publishes the reason in one line: Capacity Block reservation prices are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand. The October 7, 2026 update moves every GPU family up by the same proportion.

### AWS EC2 Capacity Block rate change, effective October 7, 2026

| Instance family | GPU | Rate before (per accelerator-hour) | Rate from Oct 7, 2026 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | B300 | $14.040 | $16.146 | +15.0% |
| P6-B200 | B200 | $12.355 | $14.208 | +15.0% |
| P5en | H200 | $6.865 | $7.895 | +15.0% |
| P5e | H200 | $5.970 | $6.866 | +15.0% |
| P5 | H100 | $5.191 | $5.970 | +15.0% |
| P4de | A100 80GB | $2.214 | $2.546 | +15.0% |
| P4d | A100 40GB | $1.475 | $1.696 | +15.0% |

Source: AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML pricing, retrieved October 2, 2026. “Before” rates are the US East (N. Virginia) or US-region rates listed on the same page; percentage change is an Axis Intelligence Research calculation.

A uniform 15% move across seven GPU generations — including a 2020-era A100 40GB — tells you this is not a scarcity signal about one chip. Capacity Blocks are AWS’s mechanism for guaranteed short-term cluster access, and a flat repricing across the whole catalog reads as AWS re-pricing guaranteed availability itself. Buyers who only need interruptible capacity should read this as a reason to look at spot and neocloud rates, not as proof that GPUs in general got 15% more expensive.

results.title: Hopper vs Blackwell: NVIDIA GPUs Compared
highlights:
Bigger chips pull more power. A Hopper H100 node runs happily in most datacentres, while Blackwell nodes run hotter and often want liquid cooling, which limits where they can live and lifts the cost to operate them. All of that shows up in the price. Hopper is cheaper per GPU-hour and, two years into its life, far easier to get. Blackwell carries a premium, and for the newest parts you are frequently waiting on allocation.

On our own rates the gap is concrete: H100 nodes start at $2.95 per GPU-hour, the H200 at $3.35, B200 at $3.75, and B300 at $4.50, all on our longest terms. Whether the step up earns its keep depends entirely on the workload, which is the decision that actually matters.

results.title: Reflection AI locked up to $7.3 billion of GPU rent inside a token price war · The Inference
highlights:
The ex-DeepMind lab's two 2026 contracts, a $6.3 billion ceiling at SpaceX and a reported $1 billion-plus with Nebius, add to more than $7 billion of rent through 2029. The open-weight market it sells into cut token prices 23% in August alone.

...

Nebius founder and chief executive Arkady Volozh. His company confirmed a $1 billion-plus compute deal with Reflection AI, books most of its revenue from GPU capacity, and lifts on-demand rates up to 21% on 1 October.

## A $2.6 billion raise carries up to $7.3 billion of rent

Reflection AI PVT$2.1B — Reflection AI, private, latest valuation $2.1B, founded in 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers, signed its first compute contract on 22 June↗: $150 million a month from 1 July 2026 through 2029, for Nvidia▼−3.21% — Nvidia, down 3.21 percent today GB300 capacity at SpaceX's▼−2.57% — SpaceX, down 2.57 percent today Colossus 2 site near Memphis. The deal is worth up to $6.3 billion, and either side can end it on 90 days' notice once the first three months pass 1.

Three weeks later, on 15 July, came a second contract worth more than $1 billion with Nebius↗, running to the same 2029 horizon 2. The company has raised close to $2.6 billion, $2 billion of it at an $8 billion valuation last October 2 3. The rent runs near triple the capital.

...

On 1 October, Nebius's on-demand GPU rates rise as much as 21% under a customer notice↗ 11. SpaceX's AI division lost $6.35 billion last year; Reflection's monthly check sits beside Anthropic's $1.25 billion and Google's $920 million, all on cancelable terms 1 5.
